title: Name ring regions and see the segments: label each region by a point, colour the mesh by part
description: User goal 2026-10-03: see the crawfish segmented into named parts in the scene before exporting anything. In the region tool, the user picks a region and gives it a name (claw_left, leg_l2, tail_3, body ...). The name is stored through CRAW-6's shared label store as a label statement selecting the region by a surface point inside it, appended to the model's .dsl, so it survives reloads and ring edits (region numbers do not: they come from ring order). The scene colours every face by its part label with a stable colour per label and shows the label names (toggleable, like ring numbers), lists the labelled parts in the controls menu, and flags unlabelled regions. Cutting out parts is CRAW-37's per-region extraction; batch export of every labelled part is a later ticket on top of CRAW-29.
definition-of-done: 1. A region can be named from the region tool; the name is saved in the .dsl as a point-based label statement and comes back on reload, including after a ring elsewhere is edited or added. 2. The mesh is coloured by part label with stable per-label colours, label names can be toggled on screen, and unlabelled regions are visibly distinct. 3. Works on fertility and on the full crawfish scan.
testing-plan: 1. Name regions on a tmp/ copy of fertility_rings.dsl and on the crawfish scan, save, reload, edit a ring, reload; screenshot the coloured parts each time. 2. Unit-test that a point-based region label resolves to the same region after ring order changes.
